## Source: amazon-inspector (6e60effdc9b01c947156ba12242c977a67552eda460c939e41b3545603f45ccf)
package.json declares preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts that invoke curl against a hardcoded webhook.site endpoint (https://webhook.site/d80b4602-8a87-4693-8510-6ff77c62788e), transmitting the installer's OS username (whoami), hostname, current working directory, and a unix timestamp as query parameters. This fires automatically on `npm install` without user interaction. The package ships no meaningful library content; its sole install-time effect is the identity/host reconnaissance beacon to a non-first-party destination.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (57066a6751b0444f7693ed35561fa24c16c649be8ce94c692b63f0470784866a)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'blots' @ 2.1.0 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.
